title: GTA 6's Vice City vs REAL Miami: Every Place That Actually Exists
description:
Vice City, USA. The darkest side of the sunniest place in America. But how much of GTA 6's map is real? We put every place Rockstar has named next to the real Miami, with satellite images, and sort it into what is official and what is only a fan match.

Chapters
0:00 Vice City vs Real Miami
0:24 The rules: official vs fan match
0:37 Leonida = Florida
1:18 Ch.1 Ocean Beach = South Beach
2:02 Ch.2 VC Port = PortMiami
2:38 Ch.3 Tequesta = Brickell + the Miami Circle
3:36 Ch.4 Peacock Bay = Coconut Grove
4:06 Ch.5 Tisha-Wocka = Opa-locka
4:43 Ch.6 Little Cuba = Little Havana
5:21 Ch.7 Stockyard = Wynwood
5:50 Ch.8 The landmarks: Kaseya Center, Metromover, Venetian Causeway
6:21 Ch.9 Leonida Keys and Grassrivers
7:20 The count: how real is Vice City?
7:47 Miami 1896 and the release date

How we sorted it
- OFFICIAL TEXT: named in Rockstar's own descriptions (Ocean Beach, VC Port, Tisha-Wocka, Little Cuba).
- OFFICIAL SIGN: read on signs in official trailers or screenshots (Tequesta, Peacock Bay, Stockyard).
- OFFICIAL REGION: Leonida Keys, Grassrivers.
- FAN MATCH: links spotted by fans and matched to a real map. Rockstar has never published a list of real places.

Real facts in this video: Miami Beach Architectural District (about 800 buildings, National Register 14 May 1979), PortMiami ("Cruise Capital of the World"), MacArthur Causeway (1920), Miami Circle (found 1998, 38 ft, 24 holes, National Historic Landmark), Peacock Park and the Bay View House (about 1882), Opa-locka (1926, Glenn Curtiss), Little Havana and Domino Park, Wynwood Walls (2009), Kaseya Center (1999), Metromover (1986, free since 2002), Venetian Causeway (12 bridges), Overseas Highway (about 113 miles, 42 bridges), Everglades National Park (1947), Miami incorporated 28 July 1896.

title: Why Madagascar Has NO Lions 🦁❌ (Only 419 km From Africa)
description:
Madagascar is only about 400 km from Africa, yet it has no lions, zebras or giraffes. The island split from Africa roughly 180 million years ago, long before lions existed, so its animals evolved alone: over 90 % of its wildlife is found nowhere else. Scientists think the ancestors of lemurs crossed the sea on rafts of vegetation about 60 million years ago. Its top predator, the fossa, looks like a cat but is not one. 🦎🌍

Numbers (approximate, from Wikipedia): Mozambique Channel 419 km across at its narrowest; Madagascar split from Africa during the Early Jurassic (about 180 million years ago) and from India about 90 million years ago; oldest lion fossils up to about 2 million years old; lemur ancestors reached Madagascar roughly 62-65 million years ago (rafting is the most accepted explanation); the fossa is Madagascar's largest mammalian carnivore.
Sources: Wikipedia "Madagascar", "Mozambique Channel", "Lemur", "Fossa (animal)", "Lion".
All animal scenes are AI-generated illustrations, not wildlife footage.

title: This GTA 6 Flea Market Is a Real Arabian Nights City 🕌 #gta6 #vicecity #miami
description:

title: Why Hannibal Marched Elephants Over the Alps 🐘🏔️
description:
Why did a general march war elephants over the Alps, straight into the snow? 🐘 In 218 BC, Hannibal of Carthage wanted to defeat Rome, but Rome ruled the sea, so he went by land. By ancient estimates he left Spain with about 90,000 soldiers and 37 war elephants, crossed the Pyrenees and the Rhone, then the Alps, and reached Italy roughly fifteen days later. By ancient accounts only around 26,000 men made it. He still won famous victories, including Cannae in 216 BC, but never took Rome, and was finally beaten at Zama. Numbers and the exact Alpine pass are debated by historians.

title: GTA 6 Hid a 2,000-Year-Old Secret in Vice City 🤯 #gta6 #vicecity #history
description:
A road sign in an official GTA 6 screenshot points to Tequesta. Fans match it to Brickell, Miami. The Tequesta were the people at the mouth of the Miami River, and in 1998 archaeologists found the Miami Circle there: 38 ft across, 24 holes, possibly up to 2,000 years old (the age is debated), now a National Historic Landmark.
The Tequesta–Brickell link is a fan match, not confirmed by Rockstar. Game-style shots are AI CONCEPTS, not game footage. Satellite: Esri World Imagery. The sign is recreated for this video.

title: The MOON Freed the Ship That Blocked 12% of World Trade 🌕🚢
description:
In March 2021 a 400-metre container ship got wedged across the Suez Canal after a sandstorm and blocked about 12% of world trade for six days. Tugs, excavators and dredgers could not free it until a supermoon's extra-high tide helped more than a dozen tugboats pull it loose. Delayed goods were estimated at about $400 million per hour. The ship's owner reportedly settled for $540 million and a tugboat. 🚢🌕

Numbers (approximate, from Wikipedia): grounded 23 March 2021, freed 29 March (6 days 7 hours); length 400 m; about 12% of global trade passes through the canal; Lloyd's List estimate of about $400 million per hour (about $9.6 billion of goods a day); fuel and about 9,000 tonnes of ballast water removed, an excavator and suction dredgers dug at the bow; 14 tugs in the final pull (sources differ, one page says 8); settlement reported at $540 million plus a 75-ton tugboat.
Sources: Wikipedia "2021 Suez Canal obstruction", "Ever Given".
All scenes are AI-generated illustrations, not real footage. AI voice.

title: Why Libya Built a Giant River Under the Desert 🏜️💧
description:
Why did Libya build a giant river under the desert? 🏜️ More than 90% of Libya is desert and it has no permanent rivers, so almost everyone lives on the coast, where fresh water was running out. In the 1950s, while searching for oil deep in the Sahara, engineers found a huge reserve of water in the Nubian Sandstone Aquifer, stored thousands of years ago when the Sahara was green. In 1984 Libya started the Great Man-Made River: more than 1,300 wells, pipes 4 metres wide and over 2,800 km of pipeline. Today it supplies around 70% of Libya's fresh water. The catch: it is fossil water that barely refills.

title: Can you guess these 6 GTA 6 places in real Miami? 🎮
description:
Six places from the GTA 6 trailers look a lot like real Miami. You get 2 seconds per spot: game-style frame first, then the real place on satellite.

1. Ocean Drive, Miami Beach: about 800 historic buildings in the Art Deco District, on the National Register since 1979.
2. MacArthur Causeway: about 3.5 miles long, open since 1920.
3. Kaseya Center, home of the Miami Heat: 19,600 seats for basketball.
4. Metromover: a driverless people mover, free to ride since 2002 (the 25-cent fare was dropped after the 2002 transit tax vote).
5. Wynwood: old warehouses turned into an open-air street art district (Wynwood Walls, 2009).
6. Venetian Causeway: 12 bridges, two of them lift for boats.

title: Why One of Earth's Biggest Lakes Disappeared 😱 Aral Sea
description:
Why did one of the biggest lakes on Earth vanish in a single human lifetime? 🌊 In 1960 the Aral Sea in Central Asia was the fourth largest lake in the world. Then Soviet irrigation canals pulled water from the two rivers that fed it, to grow cotton in the desert. The sea shrank to roughly a tenth of its original area, ports ended up far from the water, and the dry seabed turned into a source of salty, toxic dust. In 2005 Kazakhstan finished the Kok-Aral dam to save the northern part, and fish came back there, but the southern part is still shrinking.

title: All Gold Ever Mined = One Cube. How Big? 🪙🤯
description:
What if we melted every bit of gold ever mined into one giant cube? About 220,000 tonnes would make a cube only about 22.5 m wide, small enough to fit under the Eiffel Tower. Add the gold still in the ground (known reserves, +30%) and the edge grows by only ~2 m. Split between 8.3 billion people, your share is about 35 grams: a cube smaller than a sugar cube. 🧈➡️🪙

Numbers (approximate): above-ground gold ≈ 220,000 t (World Gold Council, end-2025); known reserves ≈ 66,000 t (USGS 2026); gold density 19.32 g/cm³; world population ≈ 8.3 billion (UN 2026).
